operations.specification: Defines the registration flow for new users in the Todo List system. This operation allows individuals to register by providing a valid, unique email and a password, which is securely hashed and stored in the 'todo_list_users' table. The 'email' field is unique and serves as the account identifier; 'password_hash' stores the cryptographically hashed password. No soft delete or status indicator fields exist, so all accounts are either present or permanently deleted. Upon successful registration, a verification email must be sent, and the user is marked pending verification. The endpoint only permits registration if the email is not already in use. The creation and update timestamps ('created_at', 'updated_at') are recorded, aligning with audit requirements. Registration cannot proceed if the email exists or fails business validation, and responses document error scenarios. No administrative role or escalation applies; each account is equal and manages only its own Todos.
operations.description:
This endpoint facilitates secure new user registration by creating a new entry in the 'todo_list_users' schema using the provided email and password (hashed before storage). It enforces unique constraint on the 'email' column and combines it with standard validation logic to prevent duplicate accounts.

All passwords are stored only as hashes in the 'password_hash' field, protecting user credentials from disclosure. The registration payload verifies business requirements for email validity and strength of new passwords, also inheriting broader password policy requirements from the authentication requirements analysis.

No status- or soft-delete flags are present (see schema for 'todo_list_users'); user accounts, once deleted, are permanently erased with no recovery mechanism. The 'created_at' and 'updated_at' timestamps support auditing of registration and any later change, as required by the requirements analysis.

Upon creation, a verification email must be triggered, referencing system requirements that prohibit login unless the 'email' has been verified. Error handling captures validation failures (e.g., format, uniqueness).

Any user account created by this endpoint immediately receives a pending verification status until the associated 'email' is confirmed. Related workflows include subsequent login, email verification, and password reset, as detailed in business process diagrams.
operations.summary: Registers a new user (todo_list_users) and issues a verification initiation.

requestBody.description: Information required to register a new user: unique email and password. Email must be unique and business-validated; password is hashed and persisted.

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens and user info for successful registration. Contains issued JWT and reference to pending verification.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Handles the login process for users of the Todo List application. This operation validates provided credentials (email and password) against entries in the 'todo_list_users' schema, specifically checking the 'email' and 'password_hash' fields for matches. Successful authentication results in creation of a user session, tracked in the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table, and issuance of a new JWT for the authenticated user. Login is refused if credentials are invalid or if the user's 'email' has not been verified after registration. Each session record stores 'todo_list_user_id', IP address, URLs, session creation, and expiration data for auditing. Concurrent sessions across devices are supported by design.
operations.description:
The login endpoint authenticates users by validating entered credentials against the 'todo_list_users' schema (fields: 'email', 'password_hash'), securely handling password comparison using cryptographic methods. If validation succeeds, a row is created in 'todo_list_user_sessions' for session tracking, including IP, origin, referrer, creation, and potential session expiry, as per requirements analysis and schema.

Login is strictly forbidden unless the user’s email is verified, ensuring security. Multiple sessions per user are allowed per design, supporting mobile and multi-device flows documented in requirements.

Error scenarios include invalid login (credentials do not match any user), unverified email (even if credentials are correct), and attempts to login with deleted/nonexistent accounts (schema’s permanent deletion model). The endpoint neither creates administrative roles nor escalates authority; every session is fully auditable.

Successful authentication issues standard JWTs, with payload containing userId, role, and issuance timestamp, aligning with JWT issuance rules described business requirements.

Related endpoints: registration/join, email verification, session refresh, logout, and password reset. Failing authentication returns a business error response and does not create new session records.
operations.summary: Authenticates users (todo_list_users) and initiates a new session with JWT issuance.

requestBody.description: User credentials required for authentication: email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication result, issued JWT, and user/session information if login is successful.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implements the token refresh flow for authenticated users of the Todo List application. When users possess a valid, non-expired refresh token, this endpoint authorizes the renewal of session tokens without requiring re-entry of credentials. It checks the validity and expiration of the token against records in 'todo_list_user_sessions', which track session creation and expiry using their 'created_at' and 'expired_at' timestamps, and validates that the session is linked to an active, existing user account in 'todo_list_users'.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows users with a valid refresh token to obtain new JWTs, prolonging their authenticated session without logging in again. It cross-verifies session status using the 'todo_list_user_sessions' schema, especially fields such as 'expired_at' and 'todo_list_user_id', as per business requirement for concurrent session support.

When a refresh is invoked, new tokens are emitted, and the used refresh token is invalidated (unless business requirements allow concurrent long-lived sessions). Expired or already-used refresh tokens are denied renewal. Sessions terminated by explicit logout (setting 'expired_at') cannot be refreshed.

Security and audit compliance is ensured by tying each refresh operation to both user and session records in the database for full traceability. The JWT payload structure complies with requirements, embedding userId and role.

Related flows: login, registration/join, session expiration handling, explicit logout, and security policies regarding token renewal and revocation. All behavioral logic matches schema fields and the permission matrix.
operations.summary: Refreshes user session tokens (todo_list_user_sessions) for ongoing authenticated access.

requestBody.description: Refresh token and session identifier, as required for session continuation.

responseBody.description: Newly issued JWT tokens and updated authentication information for the user.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Enables password reset via email for users in the Todo List system. Triggers a process for users to request a password reset link by providing their registered email (in 'todo_list_users'). Upon valid request, a time-limited reset link is issued to the email if the account exists. Password reset itself is finalized via a separate operation that accepts the token and new password. Respects all business and schema-defined constraints.
operations.description:
This endpoint initiates the password reset workflow for users who forget their credentials. Using the 'todo_list_users' schema, it verifies the provided email against saved user records (field: 'email') before issuing a secure, single-use, time-limited password reset token to the listed address.

No password or security answer is required to request; confirmation occurs via the reset link and subsequent operations. Underlying logic ensures tokens are never issued for unregistered emails (avoiding information leakage), and operations are auditable by email address and timestamp.

The workflow sequence includes this request phase, user action via received email, and a subsequent password reset phase (separate endpoint). This operation is public; no authorization is enforced here except input validation.

Security relies on issuing cryptographically secure, time-bound tokens and ensuring unregistered or deleted users do not leak system state information. Errors only indicate request status (always noncommittal if email isn't found).
operations.summary: Initiates password reset flow for a user (todo_list_users) via email.

requestBody.description: Registered email address of the user requesting password reset.

responseBody.description: Status of password reset token issuance. No sensitive information disclosed.

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: Completes the password reset workflow by verifying the provided reset token and updating the user's password. Utilizes the 'todo_list_users' table; password is securely hashed before storage in the 'password_hash' column. Requires a valid, unused, and non-expired token associated with the user email. Fails upon token expiration, previous use, or invalid references. After successful reset, the user should authenticate using their new credentials in future sessions.
operations.description:
This endpoint finalizes the password reset process by accepting a new password and associated token provided to the user's email. Validation logic checks the token's validity, ensures it has not expired or been used, and then updates the corresponding user's 'password_hash' in the 'todo_list_users' schema.

No direct user authentication is performed here; operation relies solely on secure possession of the issued token. Passwords are stored as cryptographic hashes, and the update is timestamped in the user's 'updated_at' as per schema.

Upon success, all previous sessions (in 'todo_list_user_sessions') may be invalidated as a security enhancement, covered by the business requirement for emergency password resets.

Errors are triggered if tokens are used more than once, expired, or do not map to an active user account (permanent deletion model).

Operation relates to password reset request workflow, user login, and security audit requirements.
operations.summary: Completes password reset for user (todo_list_users) after token validation.

requestBody.description: Valid reset token and new password for finalizing the reset.

responseBody.description: Status of password reset (success or failure state).

operations.name: resetPassword

operations.specification: Triggers a verification email to the user account after initial registration or on explicit request. Uses 'todo_list_users' for user reference (by email) and dispatches a new verification link containing a secure, single-use token. Actual 'verified' status tracking is handled in business logic and not stored in an explicit schema field in this version.
operations.description:
This endpoint initiates an email verification workflow for new registrations or when the user requires a new verification email (for example, expiry or missed original message). Uses the 'email' field within the 'todo_list_users' schema for user identification.

No changes are made to database records other than audit; a secure token is generated and used in a subsequent verification flow (external or future operation).

Input must be validated to prevent arbitrary email usage or information disclosure; requesting verification for unregistered or deleted emails returns a neutral status. Errors are silently handled, exposing no user state details to requests.

Links to registration/join, login (which is blocked if not verified), and business process requirements regarding access and account setup.
operations.summary: Sends account verification email to a newly registered user (todo_list_users).

requestBody.description: Registered email address for which to (re-)send verification link.

responseBody.description: Status of verification email delivery attempt. Result is always neutral for non-existent emails.

operations.name: requestVerification

operations.specification: This operation provides a paginated and filterable list of user accounts for the Todo List application. It operates on the todo_list_users table, allowing querying and sorting based on user registration and profile fields. Cryptographic password hashes are never returned. Each user result includes email (globally unique), optional display name, and account creation/modification timestamps. This operation is suitable for administrative oversight and is particularly useful for auditing, analytics, and support workflows. Sensitive information is protected by omitting authentication credentials and restricting access as required by the business logic.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of users who are registered in the Todo List application.

This operation enables filtering, searching, and ordering user accounts. Results are suitable for administrative views, support dashboards, or analytics. Only fields permitted by business requirements—such as email, display name, and timestamps—are returned, while credential fields (password_hash) remain inaccessible for privacy and security.

Security considerations require that this endpoint is protected and not available to client users. Only properly authorized actors, such as system administrators or support engineers, may execute this operation. The data is drawn from the todo_list_users table, incorporating key account metadata for auditing and analytics.
operations.summary: Retrieve a paginated, filterable user list from the todo_list_users table.

requestBody.description: User list search and filter parameters for pagination, sorting, and field-based filtering.

responseBody.description: Paginated response of user summary items with email, displayName, and timestamps. Password hashes are never included.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation fetches the full details of a single user account from the todo_list_users table via the path-provided userId parameter. The response delivers key identifying and metadata fields, including email (unique), optional display name, and audit timestamps. The operation explicitly excludes password hashes and other credential fields per security and business requirements. This API serves administrative purposes, enabling support, audit, or data inspection using the globally unique user ID. Only authorized actors are allowed access.
operations.description:
Return the complete detail of a specific user account identified by userId from the Todo List application.

This operation is intended for administrative scenarios such as user support, security audit, or compliance inspection. Only authorized actors may retrieve full user details. The response contains all business-relevant fields permitted to administrators—email, display name, timestamps, and account metadata. Sensitive authentication data, such as the user's password hash, is never returned or exposed in any part of the response.

Strict access controls must be enforced to avoid information leakage or unauthorized data access. This operation complements the user index/search function and should be used when inspection of an individual user is needed beyond general search results.
operations.summary: Retrieve details for a specific user record from the todo_list_users table.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user.

responseBody.description: Full detail for the administrative user account query. Password hashes are never included.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates the core authentication entity for registered users in the Todo List application, specifically modifying a user's profile fields such as email, password hash, or display name. It operates on the todo_list_users Prisma DB table. Only fields defined in the schema—email (unique and validated), password_hash (cryptographically hashed), display_name (optional), and update timestamps—may be changed. Permissions must ensure only the account owner or an authorized administrator may perform updates. User identity is validated via the path parameter 'userId', which is the UUID primary key. All changes are permanently persisted; no soft delete or status field exists by design.
operations.description:
Update details of an existing Todo List user account, identified by their unique userId (UUID).

Only authenticated users who own the account, or authorized administrators, can update a user's email address, password (as a hashed value), or display name. The operation enforces business validation as per the schema: new email addresses must be globally unique and follow business email validation rules; passwords are to be securely hashed before submission; display name may be omitted or set to null to clear the field.

Timestamps for last update are automatically persisted. There is no status or soft-delete field; deleted users are physically removed using another endpoint. Error handling addresses invalid IDs, duplicate email addresses, and failed business validations. Related operations include user deletion and session tracking for audit purposes.
operations.summary: Update a registered Todo List user account in the todo_list_users table.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user account to update, as a UUID.

requestBody.description: New values for the user profile fields to be updated; must comply with business validation rules for email, password_hash, and optional display_name.

responseBody.description: Full details of the updated user account after modifications are applied.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a registered user in the Todo List application from the todo_list_users Prisma table. The user is identified by the UUID primary key userId passed in the URL. Permanent removal leaves no possibility for recovery; there is no soft-delete or recovery mechanism by design. Only the account owner or authorized administrators may perform this action. All associated personal data and authentication credentials are completely purged in compliance with business requirements for irreversible removal.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a Todo List user account from the system, using the unique userId as a hard delete.

Only the owner of the account or an authorized administrator can delete a user. Once deleted, all personal user data including email, password hash, and display name are erased from the database. This action is irreversible—no restoration or soft delete is supported. The operation is strictly limited to one account at a time.

Error handling includes checking for valid userId format, existence of the user record, and proper permissions. Related session information (from session table) is to be handled in backend business logic if user deletion cascades are needed.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a Todo List user account from the todo_list_users table by UUID.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user account to delete, as a UUID.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation allows searching and retrieving a paginated list of user authentication sessions for a target user. It executes on the todo_list_user_sessions table, which tracks all login and session history for each user in the Todo List application. Provides session metadata such as creation time, expiration, IP, referrer, and origin URL for audit, security, and compliance usage. Accessible only through proper API authorization logic. No explicit actors are defined in schema roles, so no authorizationActors is set.
operations.description:
Obtain a filtered, paginated list of all sessions for a specific user account, supporting search on session metadata such as IP and timing. Intended for secure audit trails and compliance, the userId path parameter is used to specify the target user.

Returned data includes comprehensive session context for historical review. Direct access control should be enforced via implementation since no explicit API actor roles are permitted.

See also the detail fetch endpoint for session metadata via GET /users/{userId}/sessions/{sessionId}.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated user sessions by userId from todo_list_user_sessions.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user whose sessions are being retrieved.

requestBody.description: Session search and filtering parameters; supports metadata filters, pagination, and optional sorting.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary list of sessions matching search and filter criteria for the specified user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific user session by its sessionId for a given user. Operations occur on todo_list_user_sessions and return all session metadata fields, including IP, urls, and time stamps. Designed for secure audit use cases; session owner and API access control must be verified through business logic. No explicit actor roles are authorized at the API definition level.
operations.description:
Fetch full session details by sessionId and parent userId, for audit or security review. Returns all columns defined in the todo_list_user_sessions schema plus the foreign key reference to user.

API access is controlled by implementation, not by actor declaration in this definition. Use the collection endpoint to list sessions (PATCH /users/{userId}/sessions) before fetching detail.

Direct user access or admin/outside access must be enforced at the provider level, since actor assignment is not supported in this configuration.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed session information by sessionId for given user from todo_list_user_sessions.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user who owns the session.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session to retrieve.

responseBody.description: The complete session record with all metadata for the specified userId/sessionId pair.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation enables a user to permanently erase a specific session record from their active session history. It operates on the 'todo_list_user_sessions' Prisma table, which records each login or device session for audit and security purposes. This operation is strictly limited to authenticated users deleting their own session, not those belonging to other accounts. On success, the referenced session is immediately removed, and access is revoked if this is the current session.
operations.description:
Permanently erase a user session from the Todo List application's audit trail.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to delete a specific session record, such as to force logout a device or terminate old/compromised access. Each session is uniquely identified by the owning user's ID and the session ID, both of which must reference existing, related records as per the 'todo_list_user_sessions' Prisma schema.

Security: The session erase operation is protected so only the session owner can perform this action. Cross-user access is strictly denied in alignment with privacy and audit requirements. The business logic checks that both the provided user and session IDs correspond to a valid user-session pair; any invalid or unauthorized attempt results in appropriate authorization or not-found errors.

This operation triggers hard deletion; there is no recovery of erased sessions. Typical use-cases include manual logouts from a user's devices or revoking errant access. Related endpoints include searching the session list (for listing all sessions), and user authentication flows that create these session records.
operations.summary: Permanently erase a session by ID for a user from the todo_list_user_sessions table.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user owning the session. Must match an existing user in the todo_list_users table.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique session identifier to be erased. Must reference a user session belonging to the given userId in the todo_list_user_sessions table.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation searches, filters, and paginates the authenticated user's personal Todo tasks. It utilizes the 'todo_list_todos' Prisma table, which tracks all task objects per user with strict privacy and complex business rules. Search is restricted exclusively to Todos owned by the requesting user—no cross-user queries are supported. Advanced filtering by completion status, title (partial match), and strict pagination with configurable page size and ordering by creation or completion time is supported.
operations.description:
Retrieve and search the authenticated user's Todo tasks with optional filters, search keywords, and pagination.

This endpoint gives users robust, convenient access to their entire Todo list. Only the authenticated user's own records are accessible—business logic fully enforces per-user privacy and never exposes others' tasks. Search parameters allow filtering by completion state (complete, incomplete), substring match on title, and sort controls such as order by creation or completion date.

Security: Each request is executed strictly in the context of the user session, exclusively returning Todos owned by the calling user. The 'requestBody' allows specifying page number, page size, completion status filter, partial title match, and order options. Invalid or out-of-range values are handled gracefully, returning actionable validation errors per requirements. Related operations include task creation, detail view, update, complete, and erase APIs.
operations.summary: Search and paginate the authenticated user's todo_list_todos records with filtering.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for the user's Todos, allowing pagination, completion filter, and substring match on title. All fields optional except for per-user context handled in authorization.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user-owned Todo summaries matching the given filter/search criteria.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single Todo item by its unique identifier from the todo_list_todos table. It is designed so only the creating/owning user is granted access to the Todo, strictly enforcing privacy boundaries between users. The operation reads all business-tracked audit, completion, and content fields, fully reflecting the detailed schema and multi-paragraph documentation from the database model.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single Todo item owned by the authenticated user, based on the provided Todo UUID.

Only the owner of a Todo can access this resource. If a user tries to access a Todo they did not create, a forbidden or not found error will be returned. All information in the response—including title, description, completion state, audit timestamps, and the owner's user ID—is drawn directly from the authoritative schema in the database.

This endpoint provides exhaustive detail about the Todo, which allows integration with other endpoints such as task update or delete. The endpoint does not support soft-deletion; permanently deleted Todos are unrecoverable and will yield a 404. All field values in the response are up to date as of the most recent edit, reflecting audit and privacy business rules.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single Todo by its UUID (from todo_list_todos table) for its owner only.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target Todo item.

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the requested Todo, including title, status, audit fields, and ownership. Follows the canonical ITodoListTodo DTO.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new Todo for the authenticated user in the todo_list_todos table. Every Todo must have a non-empty title and may include an optional description. The endpoint verifies unique title-per-user (no duplicate active/incomplete tasks), links audit timestamps, and strictly assigns ownership to the authenticated user. No one but the owner may create or later access/modify the Todo. Permanent creation is logged in audit fields; all compliance and length constraints are enforced based on the strict Prisma schema.
operations.description:
Create a new Todo item for the currently authenticated user, storing it in the todo_list_todos table.

A valid request body must provide a non-blank title (max 100 chars), with optional multi-line description (max 500 chars). Newly created Todos are marked as incomplete and 'pending' by default; audit timestamps for creation and update are set to the current time according to the backend clock. Ownership is strictly bound to the creating user's account, as derived from the session context. The operation enforces the business rule that no user may have two active (incomplete) Todos with the same title. All field length and nullability constraints are enforced server-side.

If any constraint fails (e.g., duplicate pending title, too long/blank title), an appropriate error is returned and no Todo is created. Successful creation returns all Todo fields, including computed audit fields, the new persistent UUID, and ownership assignment.
operations.summary: Create a new Todo in the todo_list_todos table for the requesting user.

requestBody.description: Non-blank title (max 100 chars) and optional description (max 500 chars) for the new Todo. The request DOES NOT include audit or ownership fields, which are server-generated.

responseBody.description: Newly created Todo, including assigned ID, audit timestamps, ownership, and all schema fields.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo task for an authenticated user. It targets the todo_list_todos table, which represents user-owned todo tasks with unique per-user private visibility. The operation requires the todoId as the unique identifier and accepts the updated task details in the request body according to the ITodoListTodo.IUpdate interface, ensuring fields and data strictly match the validated schema. Upon success, it returns the fully updated ITodoListTodo object for confirmation and UI refresh.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo task belonging to the authenticated user, replacing its details with the specified data. Authenticated users may use this endpoint to change the text, completion status, or other properties of a personal todo. The todoId parameter precisely identifies the target record; the operation performs full entity replacement with strict DTO validation.

Only the owner of the todo may update their tasks—ownership is enforced in business logic, and unauthorized requests result in an error. Data validation and schema enforcement ensure all required and optional fields are handled correctly, and that changes comply with input validation rules set by the database model and ITodoListTodo.IUpdate DTO.

Optimistic locking may be used if the schema provides versioning/timestamp support, ensuring no conflicting task updates. The response provides the updated task entity, which clients can use to synchronize state. Typical error scenarios include attempts to update non-existent or unauthorized todos, or requests with invalid or ill-formed payloads.
operations.summary: Update details of a specific todo task for the authenticated user (todo_list_todos table)

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo task owned by the authenticated user

requestBody.description: Data representing the updated properties of the todo task, validated against the ITodoListTodo.IUpdate interface

responseBody.description: The updated todo task entity after all changes have been applied and saved.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently removes a todo task owned by the authenticated user from the todo_list_todos table. The operation is designed for private, user-owned todo entities, requiring the todoId as the unique identifier for deletion. Only the owner may perform this erase operation, which executes a hard delete unless the schema specifies otherwise. No content is returned upon success—clients should update the UI to reflect removal of the specified task.
operations.description:
Remove a specific todo task for the authenticated user by its unique todoId. This operation allows users to permanently delete tasks from their personal todo list, ensuring private, user-owned management and strict access control. The endpoint enforces ownership: only tasks belonging to the authenticated user can be erased; attempts to remove others’ tasks result in error.

The operation references the todo_list_todos schema definition, ensuring validation of the unique identifier and appropriate business rule application (such as preventing accidental deletion or confirming user intent). No requestBody or responseBody is required. Typical errors include attempts to delete non-existent or unauthorized tasks, or syntax/format errors in the todoId parameter.

Successful execution results in the requested todo task being fully removed from the system. Clients are expected to refresh their view to exclude the erased task and may display a confirmation message upon successful deletion.
operations.summary: Erase (hard delete) a todo task belonging to the authenticated user (todo_list_todos table)

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo task owned by the authenticated user

operations.name: erase

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: A registered user who can create, view, update, and delete Todos in their personal list. Can mark tasks as complete and manage their own account.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

pages.description:
Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

email.description: Unique email address for the new user account. Must follow valid business email rules and be unique system-wide. Used as the primary login identifier and for communication such as password reset and notifications.

password.description: Plaintext password. Will be validated for minimum strength and business policy compliance. Securely hashed before storage in the todo_list_users table under the password_hash column.

href.description: URL from which the account registration is initiated. Used for session/audit context, not authentication.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at time of registration. Used for session/audit context and security tracing. Must be provided by client.

display_name.description: Optional display name as the user's public profile name. If not provided, user profile displays only the email or blank.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Data required to register a new user in the Todo List system.

Requires a unique email and a sufficiently strong password; only hashes are stored in database (see password_hash on todo_list_users).

Includes required session context properties (href, referrer) for audit logging. Optional display_name may set user-facing profile name. On success, a verification flow is triggered and user is in 'pending verification' status. No actor ID or timestamps are accepted from the client; system manages all authentication context and timestamp fields.

Ownership, status, and soft-delete fields are not present; new accounts are permanent unless deleted via other API flows.

id.description: The unique identifier for the user account (UUID), matching the primary key from the todo_list_users record that was just authenticated or registered. Used for token payloads, frontend state, and any further user-specific requests in the application.

email.description: The canonical login and notification email address for the just-registered or authenticated user. Guaranteed unique and business-validated per user account; serves as the anchor for all identity flows and account recovery operations.

oneOf.description: User's public-facing name (nickname) for greeting and visible profile display. May be empty if unset or removed; used in messaging and list displays per UI guidelines.
No display name present; profile or UI should substitute the email address or a default value for personalization.

display_name.description:
A frontend/user-facing nickname (optional) intended for in-app display and messaging.

Null/absent if unset—frontend/app is expected to gracefully fallback to using email (never left as blank).

created_at.description: The precise UTC ISO 8601 timestamp marking when the user account was created, stored for audit, analytics, and display purposes. Guaranteed by the backend to never change after creation.

updated_at.description: The last modified time of the user account. Always set and updated by the backend for each profile-changing operation (email/password/display_name modification); formatted as ISO 8601 UTC.

user.description:
A nested, fully-detailed user profile (excluding authentication secrets) providing frontend and consumer clients with the current account state after registration, login, or session refresh.

References the ITodoListUser schema (does not leak password_hash). Used for immediate synchronization of client-visible state.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response object for user registration, login, or session refresh endpoints in the Todo List application.

Includes all user authentication result data: the user's fully-qualified ID, unique email, timestamps, and an issued JWT session token for authenticated operations. Contains a nested user profile for client state hydration, always excluding confidential authentication data (password_hash, etc). Presence of the 'token' field indicates a successful authentication operation, and the exact structure adheres to the IAuthorizationToken contract.

Describes the complete state transition at account creation or login, serving front-end needs for updating local storage, in-app context, and for security auditing purposes. The user object here is a strict superset—never a direct reference to database records.

id.description:
The unique identifier for a registered Todo List user, stored as a UUID string and serving as the primary key in the todo_list_users table.

This value is system-generated during registration, never provided by the client, and is used by the authentication, authorization, and relation mapping mechanisms in the application. The User's 'id' connects all other user-owned records, such as todos and user session audit logs.

email.description:
The user's email address used for login, authentication, and notifications.

Email addresses must be unique across all accounts and must pass business-defined validation rules to ensure deliverability and prevent disposable or non-business addresses. This field is the user's principal authentication credential, is referenced system-wide (including password recovery workflows), and may not be empty or null.

oneOf.description:
The display name explicitly set by the user for profile personalization or in-app/user interface display. May contain any Unicode text string allowed by the business, subject to max length and validation constraints.

When present, this field serves as a friendly nickname, allowing users to show something more personal than their email address in UI. Changing display_name does not impact authentication or account recovery.

Indicates no display name has ever been set or the value was deliberately nulled by the user (removed from their profile).

Null means a generic/default display should be used (such as the user's email address, or a business-defined fallback).

display_name.description:
An optional, user-defined friendly nickname for display in UI, messaging, and personalization scenarios.

If absent or explicitly set to null, the application's client or frontend should substitute with the user's email (or a default/fallback per the business requirements). This field corresponds to the Prisma nullable 'display_name' column and is omitted in non-profile or minimal responses for privacy.

created_at.description:
UTC ISO 8601 timestamp when the user account was created. Always generated by the backend; never client-modifiable.

This field is used for audit tracking, analytics, and to support business logic such as filtering or sorting by registration time. It never changes for the lifetime of the user record.

updated_at.description:
UTC ISO 8601 timestamp of the user's most recent update or profile change.

Whenever the user's profile is modified (such as changing the email, display_name, or password), this field is automatically set to the current time by the backend system. This audit field assists in compliance, security forensics, and operational monitoring.

ITodoListUser.description:
A registered user account in the core Todo List application representing a single sign-on identity for authentication, authorization, and audit.

The object contains core profile identifiers, including a unique 'email' credential (used for login and notifications), a system-assigned UUID 'id', and timestamps for creation and last update (created_at and updated_at). The optional display_name provides customization for front-end/UX, and is mapped directly to the nullable display_name field in the underlying Prisma schema.

**Security Note:** The User object never contains a password or password hash property; authentication secrets are strictly confined to server/database scope. Any additional or hidden user metadata must conform to privacy and auditability rules documented in requirements. Only the account owner or a privileged admin may access these details, and no soft-deleted/status fields exist; deleted users are hard-deleted from the system.

email.description: User email address for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all users and comply with valid business email requirements.

password.description: Plain text user password for authentication. Will be validated against the stored password hash.

oneOf.description: Client IPv4 address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR scenarios).
Client IPv6 address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR scenarios).
Null if no IP provided. Server will infer if missing.

ip.description: Client IP address for session establishment/tracking. Used for audit and multi-device security. Optional.

href.description: Originating URL (current page URL) when login is performed. Required for session audit trail integrity.

referrer.description: Referrer URL present at login (previous page). Required for session context in audit. Can be empty if direct access.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login request for the Todo List application user authentication flow.

Supplies user credentials and required session context fields. Email and password are used to validate credentials against records in the todo_list_users table. Session context fields (href, referrer, and optionally ip) are required to create a session record in todo_list_user_sessions. Fulfills all security and audit requirements for login. Session IP is optional and can be inferred on backend if not provided.

This DTO must never expose password hashes, store password in any non-plain form, or leak session/user identity fields.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token string required for session continuation and token renewal. Must be a valid issued refresh token matching a record in todo_list_user_sessions.

session_id.description: UUID for the session to be refreshed. Must match an active session and be associated with the authenticated user.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
DTO for the Todo List user session refresh request.

Carries both required credentials to validate and authorize the issuing of new authentication tokens. The refresh_token and session_id must correspond to an existing, unexpired session in todo_list_user_sessions, and be linked to the currently authenticated user. No user identity or system-managed fields may be set here.

No business data, authentication context, or timing properties are required beyond those specified.

ITodoListUser.IRequestPasswordReset.description:
Request body for initiating the password reset flow for a user registered in the Todo List system (todo_list_users).

Accepts a single required property: the user's registered email address. This triggers the backend flow for password reset and, if successful, issues a reset token to the registered email. No password or authentication is required to use this endpoint. 

The email address is validated against unique user records as described in the database schema and must correspond to a real, active user account. The logic intentionally avoids revealing whether a given email is registered to protect user privacy: requests with nonexistent emails receive a generic success response as a security measure.

Respects all email validation and uniqueness constraints described in the Prisma schema.

Used as requestBody for /auth/user/password/request-reset (POST) endpoint.

email.description:
User email address to request password reset for. Must match exactly with the unique email field in todo_list_users. This should be a valid email compliant with system business rules and the required format. If not found in the database, response will be indistinguishable from successful requests to avoid user enumeration.

Email must match uniqueness and format constraints as declared in the Prisma schema. Used as primary identifier for password reset flow.

success.description: Indicates whether the password reset operation was completed successfully.

message.description: Human-readable status message describing the outcome of the password reset process. Usually details the success state or validation errors such as token expiration or invalid reference.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetStatus.description:
Result status of a password reset attempt.

Indicates overall success or failure and provides a message suitable for user feedback or application display. Failure reasons may include token expiration, prior token use, or user account not found.

token.description: Valid password reset token issued to the user's email address. This is a cryptographically secure, single-use token that authorizes the password reset action. The token must be unexpired and unused, and must be linked to a valid user account as per the business process for password resets.

password.description: New password to be set for the user account. This is the only plain text password ever transmitted; it will be cryptographically hashed and stored in the 'password_hash' column of the 'todo_list_users' table. The password must comply with current security best practices and satisfy system constraints for minimum and maximum length. After the password reset, the user will authenticate using this password in future sessions.

ITodoListUser.IResetPassword.description:
Completes password reset for a user by verifying the provided reset token and setting a new password.

Requires a valid, non-expired, unused reset token issued for the user's email. The new password is validated and, upon success, stored as a secure cryptographic hash. The previous password becomes invalid and any current sessions may be invalidated as a security enhancement according to business rules.

No user authentication context is required; secure possession of the reset token authorizes this action. On completion, the user may log in with the new password. All activity is tracked in 'todo_list_users' and may affect session audit in related tables.

email.description: The registered email address of the user requesting a new verification email. Must match an existing user account in the system. The verification email will be dispatched to this address if present; otherwise, the result is neutral, exposing no information about account existence.

ITodoListUser.IResendVerification.description:
Request a new email verification link for a registered user account.

This operation initiates an email verification workflow, typically used after account creation or when a previously issued verification link has expired or was not received. It uses the user's registered email address to send a new secure, single-use verification token.

ITodoListUser.IVerificationStatus.description:
Represents the result of requesting a verification email for an account in the Todo List service.

Indicates whether the verification email request operation was executed. For security reasons, this response is always 'neutral': whether the email was delivered or not, it never discloses if an account exists. This schema is used after requesting account verification and for handling (re-)sends or explicit verification email requests. Actual status data for verification, timestamp, or errors is not stored. No additional account information is included, ensuring privacy and security against email-harvesting attacks.

delivered.description: Always 'true' if the request succeeded at the API level; does not confirm email existence or delivery due to privacy requirements. API always returns true for valid requests regardless of user presence. False indicates infrastructure error only, not that the user was not found.

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Query and filter criteria to request a paginated list of users from the todo_list_users table in the Todo List system.

Used in administrative dashboards, support tooling, or analytics to search, filter, or sort user accounts by registration fields (email, display name, registration date, etc). Results are paged; only allowed fields are passed (email, display name, created_at, updated_at). Credentials are never used in queries. Business logic enforces access control for this operation to authorized actors only.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts from 1. Default is 1 if not provided.

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return per page. Used for pagination. Default/maximum can be set by business logic (e.g., 20/100).

q.description: Optional query term for searching users by email or display name (partial, case-insensitive matching).

email.description:
New email address to be associated with this account. Must be unique across all users and pass business validation rules.

Leave absent to avoid changing the email. If provided, will update the user's principal login credential.

password.description:
Plain text password to be hashed by backend for secure storage in password_hash column.

This field replaces the password hash in the database. Leave absent to avoid changing the password. Passwords must never be pre-hashed or sent in any transformed form by the client – the server handles hashing before persistence.

oneOf.description: New display name for the user. Set to change the visible nickname in the UI.
Set explicitly to null to remove the display name from the user's profile.

display_name.description:
User's display name to be changed. If not present, the display name will remain unchanged.

Setting to null will remove the display name from the user's profile.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Data Transfer Object for updating user accounts in the Todo List system.

Permits modifying core user profile fields: email (with uniqueness and format validation), password (plain text to be hashed), and display name (which may be set or cleared). Only fields present will be changed.

Password should always be provided in plain text for backend hashing – never as a precomputed hash. Clients must strictly avoid sending password_hash directly. Setting display_name to null will remove the friendly nickname. Absent fields will not be modified.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for querying todo_list_user_sessions associated with a given user.

This schema provides input fields for paginated, filtered, and optionally sorted audit/history queries over user authentication/session records. Used specifically with the search (collection) endpoint for a user's sessions, it enables clients to provide search strings, metadata filters (e.g. IP, referrer), and pagination options. Restrictions ensure only permissible query options and valid formats are accepted. Title, description, and other restrictions are aligned with business requirements for audit trail use.

Used in PATCH /todoList/users/{userId}/sessions.

ip.description: IP address for filtering sessions. Accepts IPv4 or IPv6 address as string. Matches session records where user's ip field matches input; searching by IP supports both partial and complete matches.

href.description: Originating URL for filtering sessions. Filters by session href (origin) - supports partial or exact matching based on implementation.

referrer.description: Session referrer for filtering. Includes sessions matching specified referrer, possibly as substring or full match depending on backend. Useful for tracing login source or workflow context.

created_from.description: Filter for sessions created after this ISO 8601 UTC date-time value (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSX. Enables date range queries for recent/audited sessions.

created_to.description: Filter for sessions created before this ISO 8601 UTC date-time value (inclusive). Same format as created_from. Used for end-range in session audits.

expired.description: Filter for expired or active sessions only. When true, restricts to sessions with non-null expired_at. When false or omitted, returns both active and expired sessions by default, but could be restricted contextually by API implementation.

page.description: Pagination page number. Must be at least 1. Default: 1.

limit.description: Page size for pagination. Minimum 1, maximum 100. Default: 20.

oneOf.description: Sorting order. Limits sort fields to creation/expiration timestamps. Default: created_at:desc.
Sorting order. Limits sort fields to creation/expiration timestamps. Default: created_at:desc.
Sorting order. Limits sort fields to creation/expiration timestamps. Default: created_at:desc.
Sorting order. Limits sort fields to creation/expiration timestamps. Default: created_at:desc.

sort.description: Sorting order. Limits sort fields to creation/expiration timestamps. Default: created_at:desc.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
A user session record for the Todo List application.

Represents an authentication or login session for a specific registered user, recording contextual and security metadata. Used for audit trails, session history, and compliance review. Each session is uniquely linked to a user via foreign key (todo_list_user_id).

Includes IP address, origin URL, referrer, timestamp of creation, and optional expiration/end time. Supports full audit of session lifecycle. This entity is immutable outside controlled session flows, and session deletion is permanent.

Returned by GET /todoList/users/{userId}/sessions/{sessionId}.

id.description: Session unique identifier (UUID). Primary Key for session record. Used to reference sessions in audit flows.

todo_list_user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the user for whom this session was created. Links the session to the parent todo_list_users record.

ip.description: IP address of the connecting user at session creation. Used for audit, risk analysis, and compliance.

href.description: Originating URL for session. Typically the URL of the login page or API endpoint where session started. Recorded for audit traceability.

referrer.description: URL referrer at session creation. Records previous page/workflow context for security trace.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created (ISO 8601 UTC). Used for time-based audits and chronological tracing.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when session expired, ended, or was deleted (ISO 8601 UTC). Null if session is currently active. Used for session lifecycle and active/expired audits.

ITodoListTodo.description:
A user's individual Todo task with tracked status and strict private ownership.

Each record represents a Todo created and managed by a registered user. Contains required task title, optional detailed description, completion status flag, and precise audit fields for creation, update, and (if completed) completion. Ownership is enforced via foreign key, linking to an authenticated user. Enforces per-user unique active (incomplete) title constraint and logs all business-relevant modification timestamps. No soft delete; todos are permanently deleted per business requirements. Secure, private, and fully auditable.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the Todo item assigned on creation. Required for reference and update operations. Generated by the database.

title.description: Required task summary for the Todo. Must be between 1 and 100 characters in length; cannot be empty or all whitespace. Title must be unique per user among active (incomplete) Todos. Subject to business validation.

oneOf.description: Optional, user-provided longer details or notes about the Todo. May be up to 500 characters. Null if not provided.

description.description: Optional, user-provided longer details or notes about the Todo. May be up to 500 characters. Null if not provided.

completed.description: If true, this Todo is finished; if false, it is still pending. Only the Todo's owner can change this value. Marks completion status per business logic.

created_at.description: Timestamp recording when the Todo was first created. Generated and managed by the backend. Immutable after creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the Todo. Auto-updated on every change to ensure auditability and touch tracking.

oneOf.description: If completed, the timestamp when this Todo was marked completed, per business logic. Null if the task is still pending.

completed_at.description: If completed, the timestamp when this Todo was marked completed, per business logic. Null if the task is still pending.

todo_list_user_id.description: Owner of this Todo. References todo_list_users.id. Private: only the owner can access, update, or delete this record. Set by backend from user context; never provided in creation requests.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be at least 1. Default is 1 if omitted.

page_size.description: Number of Todos to return per page. Minimum is 1, maximum 100. Defaults to 20.

oneOf.description: Filter for completion state: true to show only completed tasks, false for incomplete, or omitted/null for all.

completed.description: Filter tasks by completion status. Set true for completed only, false for incomplete only, or leave omitted for any status.

title.description: Substring filter for Todo titles. Filters tasks containing this partial title (case-insensitive). 1–100 characters.

oneOf.description: Order results: 'created_at' to sort by creation time (default), 'completed_at' to sort by time of completion.
Order results: 'created_at' to sort by creation time (default), 'completed_at' to sort by time of completion.

order_by.description: Order results: 'created_at' to sort by creation time (default), 'completed_at' to sort by time of completion.

oneOf.description: Sorting direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'desc' (most recent first).
Sorting direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'desc' (most recent first).

order_dir.description: Sorting direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'desc' (most recent first).

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description: Search/filter parameters for retrieving a paginated list of a user's Todo tasks. Supports filtering by completion state, title substring, and ordering. All parameters optional; defaults provide sensible pagination, sorting, and filtering for everyday use. Must respect per-user privacy—only returns tasks owned by the session user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user. Corresponds to the primary key in the users table.

email.description: The user's email address, which must be unique and is used for login and communications. Follows standard email address format and validation rules.

oneOf.description: Optional display name for the user profile, as set by the user to personalize their experience.
Display name may be null if not set by user.

display_name.description: User's optional display name used in the UI. May be null if not set.

created_at.description: Date and time when the user was registered. Used for audit and analytics purposes.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a registered user in the Todo List application.

Includes ID, email, optional display name, and the registration time. Does not expose sensitive fields (such as password hash) or arrays of owned entities. Used in user list views, relations in other entities (as BELONGS-TO), and API responses where only minimal user context is needed.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request format to create a new Todo for the authenticated user. Provides the required title and optional description for the Todo.

Ownership, audit fields (timestamps), and todo_list_user_id are never accepted here and are assigned by the backend. Title must be unique per user among active (incomplete) Todos. The input is validated for required constraints (non-blank, len ≤ 100 for title, len ≤ 500 if description provided).

title.description: Required summary for the new Todo. Must be unique among the user's active (incomplete) Todos. 1–100 characters, not blank or only whitespace.

oneOf.description: Optional longer detail or notes about the Todo. If provided, must be ≤500 characters.

description.description: Optional longer detail or notes about the Todo. If provided, must be ≤500 characters.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request format to update an existing Todo for the authenticated user.

Supports changing the title, description, or completion status of a single task. Only the owner can update their Todos. Ownership, audit fields, and user association are never accepted or changed by client—the backend manages them. All fields are optional; each field is updated only if present in the request. Title, if provided, must be unique per user among active (incomplete) Todos. Validation and per-field constraints are strictly enforced.

title.description: If provided, updates the summary/title. Must be unique among the user's incomplete Todos and 1–100 non-blank characters.

oneOf.description: If provided, updates the longer detail or notes in the Todo. Max 500 chars.

description.description: If provided, updates the longer detail or notes in the Todo. Max 500 chars.

completed.description: If provided, marks the Todo as finished (true) or pending (false). Only the owner can update this field.

id.description: Unique identifier of the session. Corresponds to the primary key in the user sessions table.

ip.description: IP address of the user's device captured at session creation.

href.description: The origin URL where the session was started, e.g., login page or relevant entry point.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at session initiation, showing where the user navigated from.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Used for audit trails and activity logs.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated.
Session is still active; expiration time is not yet set.

expired_at.description: Expiration timestamp of the session, if applicable. Null if session is currently active.

user.description: Reference to the owning user (BELONGS-TO relation). Contains summary information only.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary of an individual user's authenticated session within the Todo List application.

Includes information about the device/IP and session origin, as well as a summary of the related user (BELONGS-TO). Does not expose sensitive data or refer to arrays of related data. Used in administrative and audit listings, API responses referencing session context, and relationship fields for session entities.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a single Todo item for list and embedding use cases.

This type provides a lightweight view focused on identification, primary metadata, and business status. It is designed for efficient retrieval of multiple Todos, such as in result lists or as referenced summaries within other DTOs.

Contains only essential public-facing fields, omitting heavy detail (such as full description or audit logs). Title, completion flags, and critical timestamps are included for tracking and status reporting. Foreign keys are summarized and access to related owner is via summary object if needed in broader API context.

Corresponds to a single row in the todo_list_todos table. Follows strict field validation rules for required and optional data, as specified in the Prisma schema and business requirements.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the Todo item.

title.description: Task summary/title. Required, must be 1–100 characters, not blank or empty as enforced by business validation.

completed.description: Completion state of the Todo. Indicates if finished (true) or still pending (false). Set only by the creator/owner.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the Todo was created. Used for timeline/audit displays.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when Todo was completed, if finished.
Null if Todo is not yet completed.

completed_at.description: Exact moment this Todo was marked as completed, or null if pending. Used for business reporting and metrics.
